featured_reviews.name: Anugraha Ghale
featured_reviews.review_text:
Then we walked into Crosswords bookstore right next door and realized Third Wave is inside the store, near the counter. There is a decent seating area there, not huge, but enough space to sit comfortably with a coffee.

The bookstore itself is nice. It’s spacious and has a wide range of books and other products. You’ll find books across many genres, along with stationery and gift items. Prices vary a lot. Some books are affordable, while others, especially imported editions, are quite expensive. It really depends on what you pick up and where it’s coming from.

I liked that there were options at different price points. You can browse without feeling rushed, and it doesn’t feel too cramped even when there are people around. The coffee inside makes it a good place to pause for a bit, read a few pages, or just sit quietly.

We were actually looking for Third Wave Coffee and found it on the map. When we reached the building, there was no sign of it anywhere. Nothing in the elevator either, so we were a bit confused at first

Overall, it’s a good bookstore to visit in Juhu if you enjoy browsing and don’t mind spending some time there. Just know that Third Wave Coffee is inside Crosswords and not a separate outlet, which can be confusing at first.

featured_reviews.review_text: The crosswords has recently become 1/4 the size as it was previously and now you cannot sit in the attached coffee shop and read (unless you purchase the book). I had an absolutely horrible experience at Liberty Book Store, Santacruz West. I was sold a burst and damaged book, which should never be given to any customer. When I went back and requested an exchange—even with a different subject book—the salesman flatly refused.
What made the situation worse was the arrogant, rude, and unprofessional behavior of the salesperson. Instead of accepting their mistake, he argued, showed zero respect, and clearly did not care about customer satisfaction. No apology, no solution, no basic courtesy.
This store has no ethics, no quality control, and no customer service standards. Selling damaged books and then refusing an exchange is completely unacceptable.
I strongly warn others to avoid Liberty Book Store, Santacruz West. Check every single page before buying, or better yet, buy your books from somewhere that actually respects customers.

featured_reviews.review_text:
On 21st September 2024 we had purchased this 6x6 Rubik's Cube from this damn Anupam stationery. They sweetly did not issue the bill and on trust we took the product. Next day some pieces poped out and when we had gone for replacement they refused to accept as we had no bill. What a scam ? Guys better buy online they never do this. Also offline stores pls don't cry "you don't get business nowadays".  This is what you do to your customers when they trust you Huh.
-–------------------------
The story continues and this time it's positive. Guys got a call from Mr.Sachin Shah floor manager on 25/02/25 (6months later is better late than never :)} Anupam Stationery and he took cognizance of the issue and has give a replacement product. All is well that ends well. I am upgrading the ratings from 1 to 3.5. I am always for offline buying it gives product with a buying experience which online can never give. Once again kudos to Sachin Shah from Anupam Stationery for not ignoring even small issues. Well Done Dear Sachin💐

featured_reviews.name: Shripad Jadhav
featured_reviews.review_text:
🚫 Bad shop, bad attitude, bad experience.

I wouldn’t even give one star to this shop. The man at the counter (probably the owner) doesn’t care about customers—only money matters to him. You could be unhappy, frustrated, or even cheated… he won’t blink.

I bought a Sequence game thinking I’d get something good. But when I opened the box at home, the board was cheap and the colors were dull—felt like it came from the discount bin. So I went back to return it. And guess what? No return, no exchange, no respect. I wasn’t shocked, but the way he behaved was even worse. Cold, rude, and zero care.

And the best part? He kept the game AND charged me ₹680 for simply opening the box and bringing it back the next day. I left the game there, walked out frustrated, and basically paid him to cheat me.

💡 Tips to avoid getting tricked like I was:

Don’t trust the packaging—open and check before you buy.

Take a friend with you if possible. Some shopkeepers behave differently when not dealing with just one person.

Try buying from places that have good reviews, clear return policies, and basic respect for customers.

Ask questions before buying: What happens if the product is damaged? Can I return or exchange?

⚠️ If you love your hard-earned money, stay far away from shops like this. No one deserves to be treated like this.

featured_reviews.name: Mehak jain
featured_reviews.review_text:
Very disappointing experience at Astoria Store.

Firstly, the person at the billing counter was extremely rude and unprofessional. The rest of the staff was also very rude and unhelpful.

We wanted to purchase 15 diffusers and requested the lady to help us get them. Her response was, “I’ve told him to get it. Yeh toh mera kaam hai bhi nahi, fir bhi kar rahi hu,” which was completely inappropriate. As customers making a bulk purchase, we expected basic courtesy.

We had a full shopping cart worth over ₹3000 and even requested assistance to carry it downstairs since it was very heavy, but no help was provided at all.

To top it off, after such a large bill, they additionally charged ₹10 for a carry bag. How is someone supposed to take their goods home after spending so much? The least they could do is provide basic support and service.

Overall, not a hospitable place at all. Very disappointing experience.
